title: dsoxlab lab.yaml (contract v1)
description: Declarative contract of one lab, read by dsoxlab from <lab>/lab.yaml. Contract version 1. Point your editor at this schema with a first line: # yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/stephrobert/dsoxlab/main/schemas/lab.schema.json

schema_version.description: Version of the INPUT contract this file follows. Leave it out and it is read as 1. Unrelated to the version of the JSON dsoxlab emits (reporting/machine.py: SCHEMA).

id.description: Unique identifier within the repository. The CLI key: dsoxlab run <id>. Discovery is by path, never by id.

title.description: English title. lab.fr.yaml overrides it for French.

level.description: Free-form level, meaningful to the repository (l1, beginner, rhcsa…). Never validated against a list.

skills.description: Skills the lab exercises. Must not be empty: validate-structure rejects it.

distros.description: Distributions or platforms the lab is known to run on. Must not be empty.

doc_url.description: Online guide of the lab, opened by dsoxlab guide. http(s) only. validate-structure --check-urls also checks it answers.

section.description: Overrides the section the lab belongs to. Defaults to meta.yml repo.category.

description.description: One paragraph, shown by dsoxlab show. lab.fr.yaml overrides it for French.

track.description: Free-form tracks the lab belongs to.

certification_tags.description: Free-form certification tags. Never validated against a list: the tool stays domain-agnostic.

lab_type.description: Kind of exercise. Enumerated and enforced by validate-structure.

exam_passing_score.description: Pass mark of a mock exam, as a PERCENTAGE of the lab scale (the points of challenge/hints.yaml, 100 by default). dsoxlab submit renders a verdict against it and dsoxlab scores shows it. 0, or the field left out, means the lab is not an exam and no verdict is rendered.

bloc.description: Position of the teaching bloc. Normally NOT written here: it is derived from meta.yml sections[].labs[]. Declaring it forces an exception and duplicates information that already lives elsewhere.

bloc_order.description: Position within the bloc. Same remark as bloc: derived from meta.yml unless declared.

runtime.description: Where and how the lab runs. Omitted entirely, it falls back to a shell runtime in challenge/work.

type.description: shell = the learner's own machine; vm = a machine reached over SSH, whose backend comes from meta.yml infra.provider. incus and kvm are backward-compatible aliases of vm; write vm in new labs.

targets.description: Execution targets, for runtime: vm. Must not be empty for vm.

host.description: FQDN, which must appear in meta.yml infra.hosts[].name.

label_en.description: Short English label, shown by dsoxlab show.

roles.description: Extra hosts used at the same time, by role. Each role becomes the Ansible group lab_<role>. Every FQDN must appear in meta.yml infra.hosts[].

default.description: Name of the default target. Must match one targets[].name.

snapshot_required.description: Take a snapshot before setup.yaml, so the lab can be rolled back.

session.description: Where dsoxlab run drops the learner: an SSH session on the target, or a local subshell for a lab driven from their own machine. Only meaningful for runtime: vm.

workdir.description: Working directory created by dsoxlab run, relative to the lab. Required for runtime: shell (must not be empty). Ignored for vm.

fixtures.description: Files handed to the learner, as paths relative to <lab>/fixtures/. The path is preserved under workdir. A file NOT listed here is NOT copied, even if it sits in fixtures/. Absolute paths and .. are refused.

services.description: Containers the lab needs while it runs. dsoxlab launches exactly the image declared here and knows nothing of what runs inside.

name.description: Short name, unique within the lab. Also the HOSTNAME other services of the repository reach it by, since they share a Docker network.

run_args.description: Raw extra flags appended to docker run. dsoxlab does not interpret them.

ready_tcp.description: HOST port to wait on (the left-hand side of ports). 0 = no TCP wait. On a published port this alone LIES: Docker's proxy accepts before the service listens. Declare ready_exec too.

ready_exec.description: Readiness probe run INSIDE the container, retried until it succeeds. A string is split shell-style; an array is taken as argv. No shell: no pipe, no redirection, no expansion.

ready_timeout.description: Seconds before giving up. Applies to ready_tcp and ready_exec alike.

post_start.description: Commands run INSIDE the container once ready (schema, secrets, repository…). Replayed on EVERY start, even on a container that was already up, so they must be idempotent.

topology.description: Historical field kept for backward compatibility. Nothing reads it any more.

validation.description: Purely DECLARATIVE. dsoxlab never reads it to decide anything: the tests are what prove.
